rules.title: RSO/JCO Relocation Assistance for No-Fault Evictions
rules.requirement: When a landlord terminates a tenancy under the Rent Stabilization Ordinance (RSO) or Just Cause Ordinance (JCO) for no-fault reasons such as withdrawal from the rental market or demolition for new construction, the landlord must pay the tenant relocation assistance, with the amount depending on household income, tenant status (eligible/qualified), and length of tenancy.
rules.key_value: Eligible Tenant: $11,000-$14,400; Qualified Tenant: $23,150-$27,400; Low/Very Low/Extremely Low Income households displaced by new development: $87,450-$115,480 (effective July 1, 2026-June 30, 2027)
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to rental units covered by the RSO or JCO where the landlord files a Notice of Intent to Withdraw or Declaration of Intent to Evict; amount varies based on household income level, tenant eligible/qualified status, and tenancy length.
rules.exemptions: Single-family dwellings owned by a natural person (including via trust or controlled entity) who owns no more than four dwelling units plus a single-family home on a separate lot are only entitled to one month's rent as relocation payment instead of full RSO/JCO amounts.
rules.quoted_span: The amount of relocation fees due to the tenant by the landlord depends on whether there will be a Protected Unit demolished for the purpose of new construction and whether household is lower income or above low income.

coverage.other_unknown_factor: whether the household is low/very low/extremely low income or above low income, whether the tenant is 'eligible' or 'qualified', and whether displacement is for demolition for new construction (triggering different, often higher, relocation amounts)

rules.conflict_note: The bulletin notes landlords must pay the highest amount required by overlapping State (Housing Crisis Act / Govt Code 66300.6) and City (RSO/JCO) relocation rules; actual amounts owed may differ under Option 3 if state law requires supplementation.
